page: Vultr vc2-8c-32gb is a General Purpose virtual machine from the Cloud Compute family. It features an Intel x86_64 processor with 8 shared vCPUs, mapped from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz and includes 32 KB L1d cache, 4 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled as a 640 GB NVMe SSD, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data reveals a performance profile heavily influenced by the shared CPU allocation. Single-core performance is limited, with stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 10%. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, as shown by stress-ng multi-core and Passmark CPU scores. Memory read bandwidth is average, reaching 516.53 GB/sec for cached small blocks, but write bandwidth for large blocks is poor. Cryptographic and decompression workloads show weak to average performance, while Redis SET operations perform at an average rate of 7.55 million operations per second.

Given its shared CPU architecture, this server offers a cost-effective option for workloads requiring a substantial memory footprint and local NVMe storage without requiring sustained, dedicated single-core CPU performance. It is suited for multi-threaded applications, general-purpose web serving, development environments, and database caching layers where resource density is prioritized over raw compute speed.
